o: Destruction to come upon Edom. Their offences against Jacob.
The restoration of the Jews, and their flourishing state in the latter times.
bg: Consists of one chapter, "concerning Edom," its impending doom (1:1-16), and the restoration of Israel (1:17-21). This is the shortest book of the Old Testament.
Idumea (Isa. 34:5, 6; Ezek. 35:15). "The field of Edom" (Gen. 32:3), "the land of Edom" (Gen. 36:16), was mountainous (Obad. 1:8, 9, 19, 21).
ch.s: This chapter covers: Destruction to come upon Edom. Their offences against Jacob (vv. 1–16); The restoration of the Jews, and their flourishing state in the latter times (vv. 17–21). People named: Esau, Jacob, Obadiah, Teman, Joseph, Ephraim. Places: Edom, Jerusalem, Zion, Judah, Philistines.
q: Read verses 1–16 (Destruction to come upon Edom. Their offences against Jacob). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 17–21 (The restoration of the Jews, and their flourishing state in the latter times), what do you learn about wisdom?
Verse 17 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Amos 9:11–15. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Esau’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Obadiah?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: In reflecting on ourselves, it is good to consider what we should have done; to compare our practice with the Scripture rule.
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.
